traveler: Auguste Kerckhoffs (Jean Guillaume Auguste Victor Alexandre François Hubert Kerckhoffs)
title: The Six Desiderata: a German Master Between Limburg, Volapük, and a Station Platform on Lake Thun
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Nieuwenhof and the Abbey School

stops.name: Nuth, birth at the Nieuwenhof
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Nuth civil birth register. Kerckhoffs's own Latin curriculum vitae of 1876 gives 31 January instead; the twelve-day discrepancy between his self-report and his village register is not resolved by any source, and both dates are carried here.
stops.campa: A son is born at the Nieuwenhof, a lease farm on the fields outside Nuth in Dutch Limburg, to Jean Guillaume Kerckhoffs, clerk-registrar and later mayor of the village, and to Jeannette Elisabeth Lintjens. The register takes down the whole of it: Jean Guillaume Auguste Victor Alexandre François Hubert. Forty-one years on, composing his own Latin vita for a German faculty, he will write the thirty-first of January instead. The clerk's son misdates himself by twelve days. The farmhouse is pulled down in 1934 to make room for a motorway.
suggested_refs: The Nuth civil birth register entry of 19 January 1835, reproduced in the 2020 archival study
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), eprint.iacr.org/2020/556, citing Nuth civil-status records

stops.name: Kerkrade, the boarding school at Rolduc
stops.date_confidence: attested; the school results table in the 2020 study covers October 1847 to August 1852. The month within 1847 is the study's, the day is a convention.
stops.campa: He boards five years at the abbey school of Rolduc, an hour from Aachen, in a house of Augustinian canons where the day is cut into bells. Latin, German and French are taught here, and they are the languages he will go on teaching for the next forty years. The surviving results show a steady boy and never a first: second prizes, third prizes, a place partway down every list. In one examination he stands fourth of fourteen and is put back to seventh. The register gives the reason: conduct not entirely satisfactory.
suggested_refs: The Rolduc examination results, Kerkrade municipal archive, table 2 of the 2020 study
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing Rolduc school records

stops.name: Maastricht, a year at the gymnasium
stops.date_confidence: attested by his own 1876 Latin vita, which gives the year only; the month is a convention for the start of a school year.
stops.campa: He passes a year at the gymnasium of Maastricht, the provincial capital, thirty kilometres from the farm. The whole of the record for that year is a single line in his own Latin. Biographers working from short notices will hand the town his birth as well, and the error runs a hundred years through encyclopedias and cryptography histories alike: Kerckhoffs of Maastricht, born in a city he only studied in. Nobody opens the register at Nuth until 1998. Nobody prints what it says until 2020.
suggested_refs: Kerckhoffs's 1876 Latin curriculum vitae, submitted to the faculty at Tübingen
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), quoting Kerckhoffs's 1876 Latin vita

segments.name: Philosophy, Natural Science, and the First Classrooms

stops.name: Liège, two years of philosophy
stops.date_confidence: attested by his 1876 vita for the years 1853-1855; the month is a convention for the academic year. Older biographies inflate this into a degree or a doctorate; the archival study finds only coursework documented.
stops.campa: Two years of philosophy at the University of Liège, across a border that in Limburg is more an administrative habit than a frontier. He is eighteen and he is not yet anything in particular. Later biographers, wanting a title to hang on him early, turn these two years into a Liège degree and sometimes into a Liège doctorate. The archives hold neither. What survives is a record of attendance for 1853 to 1855 and nothing else: no examination result, no thesis. He leaves at twenty for a Catholic university in another country.
suggested_refs: The University of Liège faculty of philosophy, 1853-1855
sources: Kerckhoffs's 1876 Latin curriculum vitae, per Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache (2020)

stops.name: Leuven, natural sciences
stops.date_confidence: attested by his 1876 vita for 1855-1857; month conventional.
stops.campa: Two years of natural sciences at the Catholic University of Leuven. The formation is now philosophy, then physical science, and it will end, twenty years from here, in German philology. He is twenty-two when he leaves, with no degree and no profession. Nothing in the record suggests he has yet seen a cipher, a cryptogram, or a coded dispatch of any kind. Whatever brings him to that subject happens somewhere the surviving papers do not cover, and no source reached names the year or the occasion.
suggested_refs: The Catholic University of Leuven, faculty of sciences, 1855-1857
sources: Kerckhoffs's 1876 Latin curriculum vitae, per Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache (2020)

stops.name: Eindhoven, the first classrooms
stops.date_confidence: attested by his 1876 vita for 1857-1860; the 'cum laude' on the public examinations is his own characterization in that vita, not an independent record. Month conventional.
stops.campa: He sits the public examinations, passes them, and reports in his own vita that he passes them with distinction. Then three years teaching modern languages in Eindhoven. It is the last post he will hold on Dutch soil. Nothing in the surviving papers explains why he leaves it. At twenty-five he packs up and crosses into France with no position waiting for him, and he stays, with two long German interruptions, for the remaining forty-three years of his life.
suggested_refs: Kerckhoffs's own account of the public examinations, 1876 Latin vita
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), quoting Kerckhoffs's 1876 Latin vita

stops.name: Meaux, the crossing into France
stops.date_confidence: attested by his 1876 vita for 1860-1863; month conventional. The Victor Hugo correspondence is reconstruction only: the source that reports it calls it reported, cautions that it establishes no close friendship or frequent meetings, and no primary confirmation was found.
stops.campa: Three years at a private institution in Meaux, his first post in France, in a cathedral town on the Marne forty kilometres east of Paris. From about this time a press item and a later line of his own are said to indicate that he knows and writes to Victor Hugo, then eighteen years into the Guernsey exile and answering letters from strangers by the sackful. The claim survives only as a report, and nobody has produced the letters. Did a provincial schoolmaster of twenty-five write to Hugo, and did Hugo write back? The record does not say.
suggested_refs: The reported Kerckhoffs correspondence with Victor Hugo, circa 1860, unconfirmed in any primary source
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020)

segments.name: Melun: Ten Years at the Collège

stops.name: Melun, appointed to the collège
stops.date_confidence: attested by the French Ministry of National Education archives. The coordinate is that of the historic collège, now the site of the Lycée Jacques Amyot, 67 rue du Général de Gaulle.
stops.campa: Appointed English and German teacher at the collège de Melun, a post he holds nine and a half years. He substitutes in Latin, Greek, history and mathematics as the timetable requires, and the administrative reports praise his learning and his method while noting, then and later, that his classrooms are noisy. In 1867 the departmental council lets him give a free winter course in English to whoever turns up. He is unpaid secretary-librarian of the Société d'encouragement à l'instruction across the same years, and the prefectural report of 1870 lists both.
suggested_refs: The Kerckhoffs personnel file, Archives nationales, French Ministry of National Education
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing French Ministry of National Education archives and the 1870 prefectural report

stops.name: Paris, the marriage in the tenth arrondissement
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Paris marriage act reproduced in the 2020 study. The kinship is fixed by the study's footnote 21 and by Le Figaro of 10 October 1888: Marie Émilie is Santerre's granddaughter, not his great-granddaughter, a slip that circulates in the secondary literature.
stops.campa: At the mairie of the tenth arrondissement he marries Marie Émilie Thévenin, daughter of a bailiff, born at Coulommiers three weeks after himself. Her mother is Émilie Delphine Santerre, and her mother's father is the general Antoine Joseph Santerre, who commanded the Paris National Guard on the scaffold morning of January 1793 and gave the order for the drums that covered the last words of Louis XVI. The Dutch schoolmaster marries into the Revolution at one remove. Le Figaro is still calling her the general's granddaughter in October 1888.
suggested_refs: The Paris marriage act of 5 July 1864, tenth arrondissement, reproduced in the 2020 study
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), reproducing the Paris marriage act and footnote 21
Le Figaro, 10 October 1888

stops.name: Melun, the birth on the quai d'Almont
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Melun birth register. The house is gone, replaced by a modern building; the 2020 study locates the site at the crossroads of the rue des Trois Moulins and the boulevard de l'Almont, and the coordinate marks that junction.
stops.campa: At one in the morning, in the house at 23 quai d'Almont, Marie Émilie gives birth to Wilhelmine Émilie Pauline. There will be no others. The girl grows up in a schoolmaster's house on the water at the edge of Melun, learns her father's languages, and will in time hold a teaching certificate in an artificial language invented by a Baden priest. She dies at twenty-seven in a rented room in the fifth arrondissement of Paris, ten years before her father, and the cause is not written anywhere.
suggested_refs: The Melun birth register entry of 13 May 1865, reproduced in the 2020 study
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), reproducing the Melun birth register

stops.name: Melun, the National Guard and the petition for domicile
stops.date_confidence: attested: the petition under Article 13 is dated 16 March 1870 and the authorization 23 May 1870; the National Guard service is certified in the 1873 prefectural report, which gives the year but not the dates of service. The stop is pinned at the collège, his place of work through the war.
stops.campa: Six weeks before the war he petitions the Minister of Justice for authorization to establish legal residence in France under Article 13 of the Napoleonic Code. It is granted on the twenty-third of May. Then the Prussians come, and the Dutch subject who has just asked France to keep him registers in the National Guard at Melun. He serves out the war in the prison service, consistently, the prefect will later certify, guarding a French jail against the army of the country whose language he teaches. He is thirty-five. The certificate of 1873 gives the year of that service and not the dates.
suggested_refs: The prefectural naturalization reports of 1870 and 1873, Seine-et-Marne
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing his Article 13 petition and quoting the 1870 and 1873 prefectural reports

stops.name: Melun, leave granted and citizenship decreed
stops.date_confidence: attested: departure on leave 5 March 1873, Council of State decree 19 November 1873, publication 11 December 1873. The stop is dated to the departure and carries both later events.
stops.campa: On the fifth of March he stops teaching at Melun, on leave at his own request, to go and study in Germany. Rumours follow him out of the town: that a man leaving for Germany three years after the war has dealings with the enemy. The prefect investigates and declares them unfounded. In November the Council of State rules that he is entitled to the rights of a French citizen. The decree is published on the eleventh of December, nine months after he left the town that had wondered whether he was a Prussian.
suggested_refs: The naturalization decree of 19 November 1873, published 11 December 1873
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), quoting the 1873 prefectural report

stops.name: Bonn, tutor to the young count
stops.date_confidence: attested: the study's career table gives Bonn as the place of the São Mamede tutoring, 1873-1880, and the body text places the household there. Month conventional. The Knight of the Order of Christ is reported by the Venloosch weekblad of 8 August 1874; the Commander rank was registered at Lisbon on 11 August 1879, confirmed to the researchers by the Instituto dos Arquivos Nacionais in 1998.
stops.campa: He settles the family in Bonn and lives by tutoring Rodrigo Pereira Felício de São Mamede, a young Portuguese count who will end as secretary to the king of Portugal. For teaching an aristocracy its verbs, Portugal makes him a Knight of the Order of Christ in 1874, Commander of the same order in 1879, and Officer of the Military Order of Saint James of the Sword. Neither the Netherlands nor France has given him a distinction of any kind. He teaches two more São Mamede sons until 1880.
suggested_refs: The Order of Christ registration, Instituto dos Arquivos Nacionais, Lisbon, Ministério do Reino, liv. 917, fl. 136v-137
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), pp. 19 and career table 3
Venloosch weekblad, 8 August 1874

stops.name: Rhondorf, the Belle Vue on the Rhine bank
stops.date_confidence: attested only by footnote 18 of the 2020 study, which records the lodging without a date; the year here orders the segment. The coordinate is the Rhine bank at Rhondorf, matching the study's own figure caption; the hotel closed in 2008 and was converted to housing.
stops.campa: During the German years he lodges at the Belle Vue, a hotel standing directly on the bank of the Rhine at Rhondorf, under the wooded hills of the Siebengebirge. The archival investigators note it in a single footnote and draw the one conclusion it will support: that a man who lodges there has comfortable means. No property is recorded, no inheritance, and no accounting anywhere in the papers. Where the money for a hotel on the Rhine comes from, when a man lives by tutoring, is a question the surviving documents do not answer.
suggested_refs: The Hotel Belle Vue on the Rhine at Rhondorf, closed 2008, figure 8 of the 2020 study
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), footnote 18

stops.name: Tübingen, the doctorate on Lohenstein
stops.date_confidence: attested by the doctoral diploma reproduced in the 2020 study, which gives the year; no month or day is recorded there, so the date defaults to the first of January.
stops.campa: Tübingen awards him the degree of Doctor of Philosophy and Master of Liberal Arts, bene comprobatam, under Adelbert von Keller. He is forty-one, and it is the first academic title he has ever held. His dissertation is on the tragedies of Daniel Casper von Lohenstein, the Silesian jurist-dramatist of the previous century, and above all on the Cleopatra. It appears at Paderborn the following year, dedicated to Alexander Reifferscheid of Bonn. The Latin vita submitted with it is the document that misstates his own birthday.
suggested_refs: Kerckhoffs, dissertation on the tragedies of Daniel Casper von Lohenstein (Paderborn, 1877)
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), reproducing the doctoral diploma

segments.name: Paris: the Chair and the Six Desiderata

stops.name: Neuilly-sur-Seine, 11 boulevard du Château
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year 1876 by residence records cited in the 2020 study; month conventional. Coordinate is the OSM geocode of the boulevard du Château.
stops.campa: The family comes back to France with the doctorate and takes a residence at 11 boulevard du Château in Neuilly, just outside the western wall of Paris. He is a doctor of the German university system, a naturalized Frenchman, a knight of a Portuguese order, and unemployed in the country he has chosen. It will be five years before anyone in France gives him a chair, and nothing survives from those five years about ciphers. He is forty-one, and he lives on the boulevard du Château with his wife and his daughter of eleven.
suggested_refs: Residence records for 11 boulevard du Château, Neuilly-sur-Seine, 1876
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), p. 19

stops.name: Paris, the chair at the Polytechnique refused
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1880 by the 2020 study and its appendix A; no month recorded. The reported administrative error over his nationality is the study's own wording. A claim that he also applied to the École Militaire Supérieure in 1878 appears in David Kahn's Codebreakers and nowhere in the archival study; Kahn was not reachable in this run and the claim is not asserted here.
stops.campa: He applies for the chair of German at the École Polytechnique, then still on the Montagne Sainte-Geneviève behind the Panthéon, and is not accepted. The reason reported is an administrative error about his nationality, seven years after the Council of State settled it, and no file survives that gives another ground. The school trains the officers of the French artillery and engineers. Three years from now their own service journal will print his article telling that army its cipher dictionary should be condemned.
suggested_refs: The old École Polytechnique, 5 rue Descartes, Paris
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), p. 19 and appendix A

stops.name: Paris, the German chair at HEC
stops.date_confidence: attested: 'From November 1, 1881, until July 14, 1891, he teaches at the HEC School', 2020 study p. 24; the Malesherbes address is footnote 36. Coordinate is the OSM geocode of 108 boulevard Malesherbes.
stops.campa: He obtains the chair of German at the École des hautes études commerciales, then housed at 108 boulevard Malesherbes, and holds it exactly nine years, eight months and thirteen days. It is the only stable institutional position of his life. Everything he is now known for is written from this address: the two-part article of 1883, the Volapük manifesto, the course, the dictionary, the reform grammar. He is forty-six when he takes the chair and fifty-six when the school lets him go.
suggested_refs: The HEC administrative file on Kerckhoffs, appendices C.2 and C.3 of the 2020 study
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), p. 24 and footnote 36

stops.name: Paris, the École Arago at the Place de la Nation
stops.date_confidence: attested by the CTHS institutional notice for the period 1881-1883; no month given, so the date orders the stop within that span. The Officier d'Académie distinction is attested for 1883.
stops.campa: Alongside the HEC chair he teaches German at the École Arago, a municipal school raised the year before at the Place de la Nation for the sons of eastern Paris. Two schools at opposite ends of the city, commerce in the west and the municipality in the east, and the same language taught in both. In 1883 the Ministry of Public Education names him Officier d'Académie, citing his service to instruction and the unpaid work he has been doing for the Société d'encouragement since Melun.
suggested_refs: The École Arago at the Place de la Nation, built 1880
sources: CTHS institutional notice, cths.fr/an/savant.php?id=104063
Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020)

stops.name: Paris, 62 rue Claude-Bernard: the six desiderata
stops.date_confidence: attested: part I of 'La cryptographie militaire' appears in the Journal des sciences militaires, new series vol. IX, January 1883, pp. 5-38. The rue Claude-Bernard address is attested for 1883 by residence records; the pin is his address rather than the journal's office.
stops.campa: From an apartment in the fifth arrondissement, while he is failing to get a chair at a normal school, he publishes the first half of an article in the army's own service journal. He is a German teacher, without military rank or commission, and he is telling the French army that its cipher dictionary should be condemned. The article lays out six conditions any military cipher must meet. The second is the one that outlives him and everything else he wrote: the system must not require secrecy, and it must be able to fall into enemy hands without inconvenience.
stops.quote: Il faut qu'il n'exige pas le secret, et qu'il puisse sans inconvénient tomber entre les mains de l'ennemi.
stops.quote_source: Auguste Kerckhoffs, 'La cryptographie militaire', pt. I, Journal des sciences militaires, n.s. vol. IX (January 1883), desideratum 2
suggested_refs: Fabien Petitcolas's transcription of both parts of 'La cryptographie militaire', petitcolas.net/kerckhoffs/
sources: Journal des sciences militaires, n.s. vol. IX, January 1883, pp. 5-38
Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020)
petitcolas.net/kerckhoffs/la_cryptographie_militaire_i.htm

stops.name: Paris, part two and the Havas telegram
stops.date_confidence: attested: part II appears in the same journal, February 1883, pp. 161-191, and is reissued the same year as a 64-page offprint by the Librairie militaire L. Baudoin. The pin is the canonical Paris pin; the journal's own offices are not identified in the sources reached.
stops.campa: The February installment does what the January one only argued for. He takes a real intercepted telegram, sent from London to the Agence Havas about British military affairs in Egypt, and breaks it in front of the reader, line by line, so that any officer can follow the method. He dismisses the elaborate Silas cryptograph as too complicated for war. Then he states the rule in its bare form: the value of a war cipher stands in inverse ratio to the secrecy its handling or its composition demands.
stops.quote: la valeur d'un système de cryptographie destiné aux besoins de la guerre est en raison inverse du secret qu'exige son maniement ou sa composition
stops.quote_source: Auguste Kerckhoffs, 'La cryptographie militaire', pt. II, Journal des sciences militaires, n.s. vol. IX (February 1883)
suggested_refs: The Baudoin offprint of 'La cryptographie militaire', 64 pp., Paris 1883
Philippe Guillot, 'Auguste Kerckhoffs et la cryptographie militaire', BibNum 2013
sources: Journal des sciences militaires, n.s. vol. IX, February 1883, pp. 161-191
petitcolas.net/kerckhoffs/la_cryptographie_militaire_ii.htm

stops.name: Paris, the Société d'anthropologie
stops.date_confidence: attested for the date of joining by the society's Bulletins et Mémoires and the CTHS notice. The exact meeting room used in 1883 is not identified in any source reached; the pin is the society's institutional seat on the rue de l'École-de-Médecine.
stops.campa: Five months after the cipher article he joins the Société d'anthropologie de Paris, and he joins it under a name he has been quietly assembling: Kerckhoffs von Nieuwenhof, the farm outside Nuth promoted to a particle. The society is Broca's, and the men in it argue about skulls, prehistory, and the origins of language in the same room and on the same evening. A membership list twenty years later still carries him, styled as a former university professor. He had never held a university chair anywhere.
suggested_refs: Bulletins et Mémoires de la Société d'anthropologie de Paris, membership lists 1885 and 1903
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing the society's Bulletins et Mémoires
CTHS institutional notice, cths.fr/an/savant.php?id=104063

segments.name: Volapük: the Academy and the Schism

stops.name: Paris, entering the movement
stops.date_confidence: attested for the year 1884 by the Volapükist historian Johann Schmidt, writing in 1964, who places the entry after the first congress at Friedrichshafen of 25-28 August 1884. No month or day is recorded; the date orders the stop after that congress.
stops.campa: The year after the cipher article he joins the Volapük movement. A Catholic priest in Baden, Johann Martin Schleyer, has invented a world language out of deformed English roots, and the first congress has just met at Friedrichshafen. Kerckhoffs is forty-nine, and he goes at the thing with the energy of a man who has been waiting for a subject. He founds the French association the following year, writes the standard course the year after that, and by 1887 is head of the movement's academy.
suggested_refs: Johann Schmidt, 'Jenotem Valemapuka Volapük' (1964)
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), quoting Johann Schmidt

stops.name: Paris, the association and the manifesto
stops.date_confidence: attested: Le Génie civil of 11 July 1885 reports the founding of the Association française pour la propagation du Volapük and the manifesto. The date is that of the press notice, not necessarily of the founding meeting.
stops.campa: He founds the Association française pour la propagation du Volapük and publishes its manifesto, Volapük ou langue commerciale universelle. The pitch is not utopian and it is not literary. It is commercial: one language for the invoices, the telegrams and the catalogues of a Europe that has just wired itself together. A press claim of the period has the director of the Grands Magasins du Printemps learning it along with a hundred and twenty-one of his employees. Movement numbers of that kind were never audited by anybody.
suggested_refs: Kerckhoffs, 'Volapük ou langue commerciale universelle' (Paris, 1885)
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing Le Génie civil, 11 July 1885

stops.name: Paris, the inaugural lecture in the grand amphithéâtre
stops.date_confidence: attested by Le Correspondant, issue of 10 March 1886, p. 919, which reports the lecture and the crowd. The pin is HEC at 108 boulevard Malesherbes.
stops.campa: He gives his first public Volapük lecture in the grand amphithéâtre of his own school, and the room is full. Commerce students, merchants, journalists and a scattering of the curious hear a German master explain a language three years old. Le Correspondant reports the crowd three weeks afterwards. In April 1889 the director of HEC writes to ask what exactly these lectures have to do with the chair the school pays him to hold, and that letter sits in the administrative file with the rest.
suggested_refs: Le Correspondant, 10 March 1886, p. 919
The HEC director's letter of 26 April 1889, appendix C.3 of the 2020 study
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing Le Correspondant

stops.name: Paris, the interview in La Citoyenne
stops.date_confidence: attested: André Maguet's interview in La Citoyenne, no. 110, 1 July 1886. The interview is the only source reached for his politics; no other statement of his on the suffrage question was found.
stops.campa: André Maguet interviews him for La Citoyenne, the suffragist paper founded by Hubertine Auclert, and he says without hedging that he is a strong supporter of the civil and political rights of women. He praises Auclert by name and predicts that Frenchwomen will vote. They get it in 1944, forty-one years after he is dead. No other statement of his on the suffrage question has been found, and no statement of his on any public matter outside languages and ciphers, in a surviving record that otherwise runs to grammars, cipher tables and ministerial reports.
suggested_refs: André Maguet, interview with Kerckhoffs, La Citoyenne no. 110, 1 July 1886
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), quoting La Citoyenne

stops.name: Paris, the course and the dictionary
stops.date_confidence: attested by the 2020 study's bibliography: Cours complet de Volapük, 144 pp., Le Soudier, 1886, eight editions; Dictionnaire volapük-français et français-volapük, 319 pp., Le Soudier, 1887. The stop carries both and is dated to the later. Translations into English, German and Dutch are attributed to Caraco's 1998 sketch, which was not obtainable in this run.
stops.campa: Le Soudier publishes the Cours complet de Volapük, a hundred and forty-four pages, which runs through eight editions, and then the dictionary, three hundred and nineteen pages running in both directions. These are the books that actually sell in his lifetime, and adaptations of the course appear in English, German and Dutch, made by other hands in other countries. The cryptography article, the thing his name now means, was reissued that same decade as a sixty-four-page offprint by the Librairie militaire Baudoin, in French only.
suggested_refs: Kerckhoffs, 'Cours complet de Volapük' (Le Soudier, 1886)
Kerckhoffs, 'Dictionnaire volapük-français et français-volapük' (Le Soudier, 1887)
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), bibliography

stops.name: Munich, the Academy founded
stops.date_confidence: attested: the second Volapük congress ran 6-9 July 1887 at Munich, the Academy was founded with 29 members from 15 nations, and Kerckhoffs was elected its president. The exact congress hall is not identified in any source reached; the pin is central Munich.
stops.campa: The second world congress meets at Munich for four days and founds the Kadem bevünetik volapüka, an academy of twenty-nine members from fifteen nations. Schleyer, who made the language, keeps the title datuval, the great discoverer, Grand Master for life. Kerckhoffs is elected president, and in three years the two of them will not be speaking. The group photograph taken here is the only reliable likeness of him anyone has ever found: a bearded man in a dark coat, standing immediately to Schleyer's right.
suggested_refs: The 1887 group portrait of the International Volapük Academy, figure 1 of the 2020 study
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), p. 22 and footnote 5
Roberto Garvía, 'Esperanto and Its Rivals' (2015)

stops.name: Paris, the third congress convened against the founder
stops.date_confidence: attested for 19-21 August 1889. Schleyer had already declared the congress and its decisions invalid in Volapükabled nos. 105 and 114. The exact meeting hall is not identified in any source reached; the pin is the canonical Paris pin.
stops.campa: He convenes the third world congress in Paris over the founder's explicit objection. Schleyer has already announced in print that the congress is invalid and its decisions are void. It sits anyway for three days, conducts its business in Volapük itself rather than in French or German, and the American Sprague works the room to keep the two factions in one hall. The congress strengthens the Academy's authority without passing every reform on the table.
suggested_refs: Schleyer's invalidity declaration, Volapükabled nos. 105 and 114
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), footnote 60
Roberto Garvía, 'Esperanto and Its Rivals' (2015)

stops.name: Paris, the Glamat nomik
stops.date_confidence: attested for 1890 by the 2020 study's bibliography; no month recorded. Schleyer's rival loyalist academy held its first meeting at Constance on 18 August 1890, which is Schleyer's event at Schleyer's place and is cited here rather than staged.
stops.campa: The Academy under his direction publishes the Glamat nomik, a normalized grammar that cuts back the founder's accents, endings and irregularities. The reform is the practical man's answer to the inventor's language, and it is the point at which the movement breaks in half. Schleyer answers that August by founding a rival academy of his own at Constance, loyal to the original forms. From that month there are two academies for one language, one in Paris and one on the Bodensee, and no body above either of them to rule between them.
suggested_refs: Kerckhoffs, 'Glamat nomik' (1890)
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), bibliography and p. 23

stops.name: Paris, struck from the list
stops.date_confidence: attested by the 2020 study, p. 23, which states the removal for March 1891 without a supporting footnote. No day is recorded. The Volapükabled citation sometimes attached to this event in fact supports Schleyer's 1889 invalidity declaration and has been left there. Rosenberger's succession on 14 December 1892 is separately attested.
stops.campa: In March, Schleyer removes him from the list of Volapükists. Not a vote, not a hearing, a name taken off a list by the man who made the language. The following year the Academy appoints Woldemar Rosenberger of Saint Petersburg director in his place, and Kerckhoffs leaves both the Academy and the movement. He is fifty-six and has given it seven years, and the movement itself is going over to the newer language coming out of Warsaw. The study that reconstructs all this finds the removal stated in the record with no supporting document behind it.
suggested_refs: The appointment of Woldemar Rosenberger as Academy director, 14 December 1892
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), p. 23

stops.name: Paris, the end of the HEC decade
stops.date_confidence: attested: the collaboration ends 14 July 1891, and the administrative council's letter of 5 August 1891 states the ground. He is recorded at 17 rue Vauquelin during the following year of job-hunting.
stops.campa: At the final German examination he says something about how a ministry examiner has graded a student. The council reads the remark as criticism of the ministry's representative and ends the collaboration. Ten years, and it closes on a sentence, not on misconduct. The letter of the fifth of August is careful to say so. He is fifty-six. He moves to a room at 17 rue Vauquelin and spends the following year writing to provincial rectors for a lycée post.
suggested_refs: The HEC administrative council letter of 5 August 1891, appendix C.2 of the 2020 study
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), appendix C.2

stops.name: Mont-de-Marsan, a year at the lycée
stops.date_confidence: attested for the school year 1891-1892 by school records cited in the 2020 study; the month is a convention for the start of the year.
stops.campa: German at the lycée of Mont-de-Marsan, in the Landes, seven hundred kilometres of railway from the boulevard Malesherbes. One school year. The man who convened a world congress in Paris two years earlier is now conjugating irregular verbs in a pine-country classroom in a department he has never lived in. Nothing in the file says how he takes it, or whether his wife comes with him. The record for this year contains a posting, a subject and a date, and nothing else whatsoever.
suggested_refs: The lycée of Mont-de-Marsan, Landes, school year 1891-1892
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing school records

stops.name: Lorient, appointed to the lycée
stops.date_confidence: attested for the appointment. The headmaster reports of March 1893 and March 1895 are attested. What happens after March 1895 is not: the study's career table is garbled here and its text jumps straight to his return to Paris in 1900. Five years are undocumented in everything reached.
stops.campa: Appointed German teacher at the lycée of Lorient, on the Breton coast, at fifty-seven. The headmaster's reports call his teaching distinguished, conscientious, clear and methodical, and note that at his age he has trouble holding a crowded classroom, which the reports at Melun were already saying when he was twenty-eight. After March 1895 the file simply stops. Where he is and what he does between then and his reappearance in Paris in 1900 is not recorded anywhere anyone has found.
suggested_refs: Headmaster's reports on Kerckhoffs, lycée de Lorient, March 1893 and March 1895
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), pp. 25-26

stops.name: Paris, the death of Pauline
stops.date_confidence: attested by Paris death certificate no. 81, fifth arrondissement archives. The cause of death is not stated in the record; cholera during the 1892-1893 epidemic is offered in the literature only as a possibility, and is not an established diagnosis.
stops.campa: His daughter dies at 10 rue des Feuillantines, aged twenty-seven. She is Pauline Mowat now, wife of Alfred Armand Mowat, and she holds a certificate to teach the language her father spent seven years administering. The death record gives a name, an address, an age and a date, and says nothing whatever about what killed her. Cholera is offered in the later literature as a possibility and nowhere as a finding. He is in Lorient, four hundred kilometres west, and there is no record of whether he arrives in time.
suggested_refs: Paris death certificate no. 81, fifth arrondissement, 9 January 1893
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing the Paris death certificate

stops.name: Lorient, Ravachol's cauldron
stops.date_confidence: attested: the Interior Ministry letter of 21 March 1894 asking Public Education to consider a reprimand, and Kerckhoffs's own reply admitting sole responsibility, are both reproduced in the 2020 study. The date is that of the ministry letter, not of the prank itself.
stops.campa: Fourteen months after burying his daughter, he posts his colleague Dejean an anonymous parcel: a novelty explosive sold as a chaudron de Ravachol, wrapped in mock-anarchist newspaper clippings, in a year when real anarchists are really bombing Paris. Dejean's wife opens it. The small charge goes off and frightens her badly. Police investigate, the Interior Ministry asks Public Education to consider a reprimand, and Kerckhoffs writes admitting sole responsibility. The rector recommends no punishment and criticizes the commissioner for overreacting.
suggested_refs: The Interior Ministry letter of 21 March 1894 and Kerckhoffs's reply, reproduced in the 2020 study
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), quoting the Interior Ministry letter and Kerckhoffs's own reply

stops.name: Paris, the petition for Picquart
stops.date_confidence: attested: the 2020 study cites the published petition in Le Radical of 29 November 1898. The newspaper page itself was not fetched in this run, and his whereabouts in 1898 are otherwise undocumented; the pin is the canonical Paris pin, where the petition was published.
stops.campa: His name appears on a published petition protesting the persecution of Colonel Georges Picquart, the intelligence officer who found the evidence clearing Captain Alfred Dreyfus, said so, and was imprisoned for saying it. The affair turns on a document and a handwriting, and on an army that would rather be wrong than be corrected in public. Fifteen years earlier he had told that same army in print that a cipher kept secret is a cipher already broken. Le Radical prints the petition on the twenty-ninth of November. Where he is living that year, and who asked him to sign, is not documented.
suggested_refs: The petition for Colonel Georges Picquart, Le Radical, 29 November 1898
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing Le Radical

segments.name: Paris Again, and the Därligen Platform

stops.name: Paris, the cryptography lectures advertised
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. Newspapers of 1899-1900 advertised weekly Monday public lectures on cryptography associated with the École des Chartes and the Sorbonne, but the École's own fragmentary archive preserves no institutional file confirming any such arrangement. No month or day is fixed.
stops.campa: Newspapers carry advertisements for public lectures on cryptography, Mondays, given in the quarter of the École des Chartes and the Sorbonne. Seventeen years after the article, the subject has come back to him, or he has gone back to it. Whether the lectures were institutional, tolerated, or simply announced by the lecturer himself cannot be established: the École's surviving archive holds nothing that corresponds. An advertisement is not an appointment. No attendance record, no syllabus and no text of any lecture has been found.
suggested_refs: Newspaper advertisements for the Monday cryptography lectures, 1899-1900
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing contemporary newspaper advertisements; institutional confirmation not found

stops.name: Paris, back among the anthropologists
stops.date_confidence: attested: he is recorded in the Société d'anthropologie's account of its session of 5 April 1900, which is what establishes he is back in Paris. The free German lectures for the Société commerciale pour l'étude des langues étrangères are attested by the Bulletin de la Chambre de commerce de Paris for 20 October 1900 and 30 November 1901.
stops.campa: He is back in Paris, and the proof is a line in the minutes of the Société d'anthropologie for the session of the fifth of April. Sixty-five years old, no chair, no academy, no movement. He teaches free German classes for the Société commerciale pour l'étude des langues étrangères, in a programme that also offers Spanish, English, Arabic and Russian to clerks who want them. It is unpaid, as the winter English course at Melun was in 1867. The Chamber of Commerce bulletin records him at it in October 1900 and again in November 1901.
suggested_refs: Bulletin de la Chambre de commerce de Paris, 20 October 1900 and 30 November 1901
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing the Bulletins et Mémoires de la Société d'Anthropologie de Paris and the Bulletin de la Chambre de commerce

stops.name: Paris, 6 rue Rataud
stops.date_confidence: attested as his last known address for approximately 1900-1903 by residence records; no precise date. That he was retired by 1902 or 1903 is inference: no pension decision or retirement decree was located.
stops.campa: His last address is a building on the rue Rataud, a short street on the slope behind the Panthéon, a few hundred metres from where he was living when he wrote the six desiderata. The archival investigators note, and decline to draw anything from, that it stands within metres of buildings a later century filled with French cryptographic research. No pension file has been found, no retirement decree, no statement of means. He is sixty-seven and probably retired, and no document says so. What he lives on here is as undocumented as what paid for the Belle Vue thirty years earlier.
suggested_refs: Residence records for 6 rue Rataud, Paris, circa 1900-1903
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), citing residence records

stops.name: Därligen, the Hospiz du Lac
stops.date_confidence: attested: the Oberländisches Volksblatt of 11 August 1903 records that he had been staying at the guesthouse since 24 July as 'Professor Auguste Kerckhoffs from Paris', aged 68.
stops.campa: On the twenty-fourth of July he takes a room at the Hospiz du Lac, a guesthouse on the shore of the Thunersee in the Bernese Oberland, and the register puts him down as Professor Auguste Kerckhoffs from Paris, aged sixty-eight. He is neither a professor nor, by birth, from Paris, and both descriptions have by now been true of him for so long that no one is going to contest either. Sixteen days of a Swiss summer follow, and nothing is recorded about any of them.
suggested_refs: Oberländisches Volksblatt, Interlaken, 11 August 1903
sources: Oberländisches Volksblatt, 11 August 1903, quoted in Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache (2020), p. 28, and at plattformj.ch/artikel/30064/

stops.name: Därligen, the station platform
stops.date_confidence: attested by the Swiss death certificate for 9 August and by the newspaper of 11 August reporting an accident of two days earlier, about half past seven in the evening. Johann Martin Schleyer's diary instead records 11 August and describes him as cut in two; the two-day discrepancy is not resolved, and the diary's account of the place, Därligen station, is correct. The claim found on English Wikipedia that he died in Paris is a separate and later error.
stops.campa: On a Sunday evening, about half past seven, he walks down to the little station at Därligen to meet people he knows who are arriving on the train. He is struck by it and fatally injured. The paper at Interlaken prints the account two days later. His old enemy Schleyer writes the death into his own diary with the date wrong by two days and the place exactly right. Sixty years afterwards it is that diary entry that sends a researcher to the Därligen archive to find out whether any of it happened.
suggested_refs: The Därligen death certificate, 9 August 1903
Johann Martin Schleyer's diary entry on Kerckhoffs's death
sources: Oberländisches Volksblatt, 11 August 1903
Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), pp. 2 and 28-29
plattformj.ch/artikel/30064/

stops.name: Interlaken, the morgue
stops.date_confidence: attested that the body was taken to the Interlaken morgue before transport to Paris; the exact day of the transfer is not recorded, and the date here orders the stop between the accident and the burial.
stops.campa: The body, heavily mutilated, is carried the few kilometres along the lake shore to the morgue at Interlaken, and from there loaded onto a train for Paris, the last of the crossings between France and the German-speaking world that he has been making since he was twenty-five. Marie Émilie is told in Paris. She has a week in which to arrange everything, and on the fifteenth of August she walks into the office of the Montparnasse cemetery and buys a plot in perpetuity, concession number one hundred and forty-one.
suggested_refs: Oberländisches Volksblatt, Interlaken, 11 August 1903
sources: Oberländisches Volksblatt, 11 August 1903, per plattformj.ch/artikel/30064/ and Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache (2020)

stops.name: Cimetière du Montparnasse, division 27
stops.date_confidence: attested by the burial certificate reproduced in the 2020 study: division 27, third line north, no. 43 east, perpetual concession no. 141, purchased by his widow the day before. The pin is the canonical Montparnasse pin used across the corpus.
stops.campa: He is buried in division twenty-seven, third line north, forty-three east. The stone is small and carries his daughter as well, Pauline Mowat née Kerckhoffs, whose birth date is engraved two days off what the register of Melun says, the same kind of error he made about himself in his Latin vita. The grave goes unvisited for most of a century. In 1997 a photograph shows a white flower pot on it; by the time anyone photographs it again the pot is gone and nobody knows who put it there.
suggested_refs: The Montparnasse burial certificate, concession no. 141, reproduced in the 2020 study
The researchers' notification of the grave's historical significance to the Paris cemetery authorities, 12 May 2020, made to prevent legal recycling of an apparently abandoned concession
sources: Caraco, Géraud-Stewart & Naccache, 'Kerckhoffs' Legacy' (2020), p. 28 and pp. 29-30, reproducing the Montparnasse Cemetery burial certificate
